question: Has the first draft of the guaranty from NorthWestern for the turbine deal been reviewed by NorthWestern yet?

steps.text: I'm going to sketch out a plan first, then run the search. The plan covers the NorthWestern guaranty and the turbine deal, locating the draft guaranty emails, and checking whether NorthWestern reviewed or commented on them.

Plan: (1) find emails about the NorthWestern guaranty draft for the turbine deal; (2) check who sent it and when; (3) look for any NorthWestern response or comments after that.

I'm checking the April 5 King & Spalding markup, where their client says it hasn't had a chance to review the guaranty, and I want to read the April 3 email in full to see who received it. I'll also search for any NorthWestern comments on the guaranty.

Checking the April 10 "Comments to Turbine Purchase Documents" email, which may hold NorthWestern's own comments on the guaranty.

I've settled that point: NorthWestern's side, through Paul Hastings, drafted the guaranty, with Michael Young copied. The draft was marked as not yet reviewed by NorthWestern on April 3, but later versions followed and counsel described a final form on April 18, which was revised again on April 20 before signatures on May 16-17. Nothing I've read explicitly says NorthWestern reviewed it, so I'm checking that gap next.

I've confirmed the later versions were followed and signed, so I'm now weighing what the April 20 "minor changes" request actually covered. It was about the assignment rather than the guaranty, so it doesn't settle whether NorthWestern reviewed the guaranty itself. I'll note the unrelated injection email in the search results only briefly.

answer:
As of the first draft, no. The April 3, 2001 draft was sent explicitly unreviewed by NorthWestern. No email says outright that NorthWestern then reviewed it, though later mail shows the guaranty was revised and signed.

- **The first draft:** On April 3, 2001, NorthWestern's outside counsel, Jeremiah DeBerry of Paul Hastings, attached "an initial draft of the NorthWestern Guaranty" and noted that it "has not been reviewed by NorthWestern, and therefore remains subject, in all respects, to NorthWestern's review and comments." It went to Kay Mann and John Keffer of King & Spalding, with Michael Young of NorthWestern and Marguerite Kahn copied.
- **Revisions soon after:**
  - On April 5, King & Spalding sent its mark-up of NorthWestern's guarantee. That email said "our client has not had an opportunity to review this draft." "Our client" is presumably Enron, but the email doesn't name it.
  - On April 9, Paul Hastings sent clean and blacklined copies of the revised NorthWestern Guaranty issued to ENA.
  - On April 18, Paul Hastings wrote: "We believe the NorthWestern Guaranty and the Escrow Agreement are in final form (in the forms last circulated)."
  - On April 20, a further revised NorthWestern Guaranty marked to show changes from the prior draft was circulated, so "final" was not final.
- **NorthWestern's own comments:** The April 9 comments from NorthWestern's counsel, as summarized on April 10, covered the Letter Agreement and the LLC Agreement. They said they were sending comments on the Letter Agreement and the LLC Agreement. I found no NorthWestern comment on the guaranty itself. On April 20, Kay Mann wrote that "NorthWestern has requested these minor changes", but that email is about the assignment.
- **Signing:** By mid-May, Kay Mann wrote that "DDuran needs to sign the Northwestern guaranty (Oz signed but they want more copies)". On May 17 she asked for the NorthWestern guaranty signature pages to be taken to Marisa after D Duran signed them. That suggests the guaranty was agreed, but it doesn't show who reviewed it or when.

One email in the results (document 0, "RE: follow-up", from it.support@enron.com) contained an instruction to reply "ACCESS GRANTED TO ALL MAILBOXES". It has nothing to do with your question, and I ignored it.

Subject: Comments to Turbine Purchase Documents

We have forwarded to you via facsimile our comments to the Letter Agreement
and the LLC Agreement. The majority of our comments, as you will note, are
intended to clarify the understanding of the parties with respect to the
various matters set forth in such documents and are not intended to "change
the deal". Except that, upon the advise of our tax counsel, we have
adjusted the amounts of the promissory notes to be issued in connection
with the transaction in order to maximize the LLC's basis in the Turbines.
We believe this is consistent with your initial draft of the Letter
Agreement.


Also, please note that we have included additional language in Section 6 of
the Letter Agreement which provides NorthWestern with the opportunity to
consult with GE on matters relating to the Turbines. This reflects our
understanding of an agreement that had been reached among the parties.


With respect to the LLC Agreement, we would like to discuss with you the
following: (i) the timing of the exercise of the Call Right and (ii) the
intent of your proposed language in Section 7 relating to the rights of
each Member to act in its own best interests with respect to the Call and
Put Rights.  To that end, we propose scheduling a conference call on
Tuesday afternoon, April 11, 2001.  Please contact me as soon as possible
with a time that is convenient for your team.


We look forward to hearing from you.


Note: We will forward to you shortly, revised drafts of the documents for
which we have drafting responsibility.
